---
title: "Stage 2 — link the Biomedical Concepts"
---

Attaching the standard definition of what is measured to the points in the chain where a
measurement enters.

## What this is

A Biomedical Concept is the standard definition of a thing you measure — serum alanine
aminotransferase, say — with its units, its codes and its permissible values. Linking means
saying *this terminal of the chain is fed by that concept*.

## What you do

In the derivation pipeline, select each measure terminal and attach the study's concepts.

## What you should see

Every measure terminal showing its concepts. Dimensions — subject, visit, treatment,
parameter — carry none, correctly: they are structural, not measured.

## What to look out for

**The builder ignores the USDM endpoint-to-concept link.** This was found by experiment, not
by reading: inject a study concept deliberately *not* linked to the endpoint and it is still
offered in the terminal picker.

So the join authored in stage 1 is not the join the chain uses. Terminal-level linking is an
independent, second join, and it is the one that matters downstream. Expect to do it twice
and do not assume the first one carried.
